reports.title: Skeena Gold & Silver Reports Q3 2026 Financial Results;

desk.headline: No revenue yet; Q3 loss widens to C$52.3m as Eskay Creek construction continues; first production still targeted for Q2 2027

other.label: Spending on mine property and equipment, Q3

results: Skeena is still building its Eskay Creek gold-silver mine in British Columbia, so it has no sales yet.
The Q3 loss grew to C$52.3m (C$0.42 a share) from C$36.8m, as overhead rose to C$21.0m, mostly from share-based pay and community and environmental costs.
It spent C$117.8m on the mine in Q3 and C$321.4m in the first nine months.
Cash was C$71.0m plus C$397.8m of restricted cash from its US$750m notes, which the company expects to fund the mine to commercial production.
It made its first interest payment on the notes (C$42.9m) and appointed a new senior vice president of operations.

guidance.summary: Skeena still targets initial production and cash flow at Eskay Creek in Q2 2027, the same timing it gave in August; it gives no financial forecasts.

watch: Construction progress and costs as Eskay Creek nears start-up.
Release of the restricted cash, which depends on meeting the notes' conditions.
The gold stream completion test due by 30 Sep 2027; missing it raises the stream's share of gold.
